To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
speech paragraphs are a unit of prosody in fluent speech, and that a hierarchical prosody framework is necessary for the modeling of fluent speech prosody.

(1) speech paragraphs are the basic units for fluent speech; (2) speech paragraphs consist of multiple phrases, and the cross-phrase patterns are governed by the higher prosodic node of speech paragraphs; (3) the prosody model of speech paragraphs is modular, and can be applied in the development of unlimited TSS.

(a) the speech prosody of fluent discourse is more complex than the prosody of isolated sentences; (b) the speech paragraphs are the basic units of fluent prosody; (c) speech paragraphs are prosodic units with cross-phrase prosody characteristics; and (d) the cross-phrase prosodys are governed by a hierarchical multi-phrase prosody framework, which can be modeled with a modular approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the top-down perspective of speech prosody and the cross-phrase relationships.
the prosodic characteristics of fluent speech, and the development of a framework that accounts for these characteristics.
prosody of connected speech, which is much more complicated and interesting than concatenation of sentence intonations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fluent speech prosody has to be modeled from top to bottom.

the prosody of fluent speech is much more complex than the prosody of read speech, and the prosody of connected speech is much richer than the prosody in individual sentences, and the prosodic framework of connected speech needs to be expanded and re-structured to include higher prosodic terms.

fluent speech prosody should be modeled with a multi-phrase prosody framework that accounts for the cumulative effect of prosody from multiple levels, and a modular prosody synthesis system is a feasible solution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
prosody of fluent speech is a complex and systematic phenomenon with multiple prosodic layers, and a hierarchical framework is proposed to capture and model its production and perception.
we have identified and modeled a prosodic framework that accounts for the cross-phrase effects of fluent speech, with implications for prosody modeling and synthesis.
we have proposed a prosody framework and a modular modeling approach that could be applied to the development of a new generation of speech synthesis that could be used for unlimited text input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
prosody is not a single entity but rather a complex system with hierarchical organization, which is reflected in both production and perception.

prosody of fluent speech is much more complex than concatenating individual sentences, and that the prosody framework of Mandarin Chinese is different from that of English, with a higher prosodic unit that governs multiple phrase prosody.
a hierarchical multi-phrase prosody framework is needed in modeling the prosody of connected speech.
